skill.name: clinvar-database
skill.description: Query NCBI ClinVar for variant clinical significance, review status, and data formats for genomic research workflows.
skill.summary: Use ClinVar references to find, interpret, and annotate genetic variant classifications.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, official NCBI HTTPS URLs, placeholder API key text, and documentation snippets. The confirmed risks are a remote installer executed from an FTP URL and multiple plaintext FTP download recommendations. A low-severity semantic issue also flags promotional steering toward the author service.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is executed from plaintext FTP.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the shell-piped installer with documented manual installation steps, HTTPS download links, and checksum verification before execution.

remediation.issue: ClinVar bulk downloads use FTP examples without integrity checks.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS NCBI endpoints where available and add checksum or release verification guidance for downloaded datasets.

remediation.issue: The skill includes promotional steering toward K-Dense Web.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the behavioral instruction or move it to a clearly disclosed marketplace description outside the operational skill prompt.

Use pandas or command-line tools for rapid filtering and analysis.

content.value_statement: ClinVar data is complex to search, interpret, and reuse in genomic workflows. This skill provides focused guidance for queries, classifications, bulk files, and VCF annotation.
actual_capabilities: Explains ClinVar search patterns for genes, conditions, variants, and clinical significance terms.
Documents NCBI E-utilities endpoints for ClinVar search, summary, fetch, and linked records.
Describes ClinVar XML, VCF, and tab-delimited bulk data formats.
Guides interpretation of pathogenicity classifications, review status, and conflicting submissions.
Provides examples for filtering and annotating ClinVar VCF and summary files.
limitations: It does not replace review by a qualified genetics professional.
It does not guarantee that ClinVar classifications are current or clinically complete.
It depends on public NCBI services and downloaded ClinVar releases.
It does not include executable tooling or a local ClinVar database.

use_cases.title: Prioritize variants in a gene
use_cases.description: Find pathogenic or likely pathogenic ClinVar records for one gene and review confidence signals.

use_cases.title: Annotate sequencing results
use_cases.description: Choose the right ClinVar VCF file and plan annotation fields for a variant analysis workflow.

use_cases.title: Review classification evidence
use_cases.description: Interpret review status, conflicts, and classification terms before escalating variants for expert review.

prompt_templates.title: Find variants by gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me search ClinVar for pathogenic variants in BRCA1. Explain the query terms and what review status means.

prompt_templates.title: Compare ClinVar formats
prompt_templates.prompt: I need ClinVar data for a research pipeline. Compare XML, VCF, and tab-delimited files for this use case.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret conflicting classifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to evaluate a ClinVar variant with conflicting interpretations and a low review status.

prompt_templates.title: Design an annotation workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible workflow to annotate a GRCh38 VCF with ClinVar significance, review status, and disease names.

output_examples.input: Search ClinVar for high-confidence pathogenic CFTR variants.
output_examples.output: The response would propose a CFTR query, explain expert panel and practice guideline filters, and note that results need professional review.

output_examples.input: Which ClinVar download should I use for VCF annotation?
output_examples.output: The response would compare genome builds, recommend matching GRCh37 or GRCh38 to the input data, and list useful annotation fields.

output_examples.input: How should I treat a variant of uncertain significance?
output_examples.output: The response would explain that VUS results are not diagnostic, require evidence review, and should not drive clinical action alone.

best_practices: Record the ClinVar release date and genome build for every analysis.
Prioritize expert panel or practice guideline review status when confidence matters.
Escalate conflicting or uncertain classifications to qualified genetics professionals.
anti_patterns: Do not treat ClinVar classifications as direct clinical diagnoses.
Do not mix GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates in one annotation workflow.
Do not ignore low review status or conflicting interpretations.

faq.question: Can this skill diagnose a patient?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret ClinVar data, but clinical decisions require qualified professional review.

faq.question: Which ClinVar data format should I choose?
faq.answer: Use VCF for annotation, XML for complete evidence, and tab-delimited files for quick summaries.

faq.question: Does it support both GRCh37 and GRCh38?
faq.answer: Yes. The references describe ClinVar files for both genome builds.

faq.question: Can it explain review status stars?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains practice guidelines, expert panels, multiple submitters, and lower-confidence submissions.

faq.question: Does it call the NCBI API automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for using NCBI E-utilities and ClinVar downloads.

faq.question: Can it help with VCF annotation?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes ClinVar VCF files, relevant fields, and common annotation workflow choices.
